call_points.text: Tritium revenue expected to scale about 3x, with EBITDA losses down 25%.
Hyderabad plant fully operational in Q4; majority of Gurgaon production to shift there over 2-3 months.
Critical Power exports hit a record ₹30 Cr in Q4, 15% of sales; target raised to 20% of revenue in FY27.
Standalone gross margin expanded to 27% on richer EVSE mix and fewer low-margin lithium batteries.
Tritium's low-cost inventory runs out by next quarter, after which margins normalise to lower levels.
Inventory build-up is temporary, from Hyderabad and Gurgaon running in parallel; expected to normalise over coming quarters.
Receivables rose on late-quarter revenue weighting; management says collections are on track.
Non-telecom BESS targeted at over ₹50 Cr of business in FY27, from an insignificant base last year.
BESS scale-up depends on local cell manufacturing, which management expects next year and the year after.
Tritium remains firmly on track for EBITDA breakeven in Q4 FY27.

operating_notes.text: Exicom Power Solutions B.V. had issued USD 10 million of OCDs to a foreign investor, of which USD 5.5 million has been approved for conversion into ordinary shares.
9MFY26 consolidated PBILDT losses widened to ~₹104 Cr mainly due to losses incurred by 100% subsidiary Tritium.
Hyderabad manufacturing facility inaugurated in March 2026 with an investment of ~₹216 crore, expanding manufacturing capacity 2.5x.
Tritium delivered USD $9.7 Mn in revenue and USD $12.6 Mn backlog entering Q1 FY27.
Critical Power order book about ₹1,000 Cr at 31 March 2026, plus ₹400 Cr of opportunities being pursued.
Tritium Q4FY26 revenue about $10 million with highest-ever quarterly order booking of $10 million and sales of $9.7 million.
EV charging Q4FY26 revenue ₹88 Cr, an all-time high; exports to Southeast Asia ₹32 Cr for the full year.

Nextwave Communications Private Limited, promoter of Exicom, held 7,61,04,121 shares (54.72%) at 31 March 2026, of which 2,566,585 shares (1.85% of paid-up capital) were pledged/encumbered, with no increase during FY26.

timeline.summary: Exicom's stake in Dutch unit Exicom Power Solutions B.V. diluted from 100% to 92.23% upon USD 5.5 million debenture conversion.
Exicom Tele-Systems submitted CARE Ratings Monitoring Agency reports for the quarter ended March 31, 2026, for its IPO and Rights Issue.
Exicom Tele-Systems reported Q4FY26 consolidated revenue of ₹387.95 Cr and a net loss of ₹54.31 Cr.
Q4FY26 results (consolidated): revenue ₹387.95 Cr; net loss to shareholders ₹54.31 Cr (against a loss of ₹62.27 Cr a year earlier).
Exicom reported Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue of ₹387.9 Cr with EBITDA turning positive for the first time post Tritium acquisition.
Exicom Tele-Systems Limited shared the audio recording of its Investors’/Analysts’ Conference Call on May 19, 2026, discussing FY2026 results.
Exicom's May 19, 2026 Q4FY26 earnings call transcript: consolidated EBITDA turned positive in Q4FY26, Tritium revenue guided to scale about 3x in FY27 with EBITDA breakeven still targeted for Q4FY27.
Nextwave Communications' annual Reg 31(4) disclosure showed it held 54.72% of Exicom at 31 March 2026, with 1.85% of paid-up capital pledged and no increase in encumbrances during FY26.
